newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end sharply up on land liquidity plan.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end sharply up on land liquidity plan.

text.p: Tokyo's key Nikkei stock average closed over two percent higher on Tuesday, as market participants rejoiced over the government's decision to draw up plans to boost the stagnant land market by the end of the month which is also the end of the fiscal year, brokers said.

The TOPIX was 18.24 points or 1.34 percent higher at 1,376.99. The Nikkei 300 added 3.56 points or 1.37 percent to 263.51. The second section index, however, slipped 1.64 points or 0.10 percent to 1,640.54. Turnover was 13.04 million shares, up from 9.59 million on the previous day.

Nomura Securities Co Ltd added 50 yen to 1,390 despite news the California Public Employees' Retirement System would indefinitely stop all trading activity with Nomura within the pension plan's internally and externally managed portfolios. Brokers said the market was immune to the latest bit of news as the shares had already been battered severely.
Shares of West Japan Railway Co closed at a record high, rising 6,000 yen to 407,000, as investors hurried to buy them ahead of the end of the fiscal year and to obtain dividends, brokers said.
Truck maker Hino Motors Ltd was driven higher by news that Toyota Motor Corp would increase its stake. It added 58 yen to 780.
The mining, gas, oil, real estate and insurance sectors headed the list of gainers. The main retreaters were communications, air transport and fisheries.
